TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM EDT Sun Oct 11 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The Weather Prediction Center is issuing advisories on
Post-Tropical Cyclone Isaias, located inland over Tennessee.

Eastern Tropical Atlantic:
An elongated area of low pressure centered about 100 miles
southwest of the Cabo Verde Islands is producing a large but
disorganized area of showers and thunderstorms extending from
near those islands southward for several hundred miles. Some
development of this system is possible during the next couple of
days while the low north-northwestward before upper-level winds
become too strong for development by midweek. Very heavy rainfall
is also possible during the next few days over portions of the Cabo
Verde Islands regardless of whether the system ever becomes a
tropical cyclone.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$

Heavy rainfall associated with Post-Tropical Cyclone Isaias will continue across the Southern Appalachians and Southeast tonight. Considerable flash and urban flooding will be possible. Landslides are also possible across the Southern Appalachians. 2. Strong wind gusts continue to pose a threat across the southeastern United States today, particularly near the southern Appalachians. Scattered power outages and downed trees and powerlines may occur, with the risk highest in elevated terrain. 3. Swells from Isaias will continue to affect much of the Gulf coasts of the United States, Mexico, and western Cuba this weekend. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office. 4. A couple of tornadoes are possible tonight across eastern Georgia and the Carolinas.
